Area Forecast Discussion...UPDATED
National Weather Service Los Angeles/Oxnard CA 
815 PM PST Thu Nov 19 2026

.SYNOPSIS...19/756 PM.

Isolated showers will persist through later this evening, then 
dry weather will return Friday through Sunday afternoon. Highs are
expected to be around 5 degrees below normal. Overnight lows will
be chilly as well, with some areas dropping below freezing. Light
rain is possible Sunday night into Monday and again next 
Wednesday.

&&

.SHORT TERM (THU-SUN)...19/806 PM.

***UPDATE***

Today's strong storm system produced very heavy rain for a portion
of the day, followed by scattered moderate to locally heavy
showers. The highest rainfall amounts were in Santa Barbara and 
San Luis Obispo Counties, with the top numbers between around 4
inches to 5.7 inches. Further south, the peak rainfall amounts in
Ventura and LA Counties ranged from 2 to 3.5 inches. Peak rates 
topped out at 2.26" in one hour over Mulholland Drive above 
Encino, which statistically was a once in 100 year event. Aside 
from a few isolated showers in LA County, the rain is over and 
skies are clearing over much of the area. 

A chilly night is on tap for SW California, with many lows in the
mid 30s to 40s over the valleys, with 30s common further inland.
Even some near-coastal areas will see lows in the mid 40s to near
50. Friday and Saturday will be cool and dry with highs mainly in
the 50s and 60s. For the weekend, overnight lows will be cold, 
especially for the interior areas where some sub-freezing 
temperatures are possible, most likely in the Antelope Valley and 
parts of interior SLO County. Some light northeast winds are 
expected this weekend as weak offshore gradients develop with
winds likely topping out in the 20-30 mph range.

A very weak system will move into the area Sunday night into
Monday morning. At most maybe a quarter inch of rain along the 
Central Coast and a tenth or less to the south.

.LONG TERM (MON-THU)...19/122 PM.

The rest of Monday and Tuesday will be dry with a slow warming
trend. 

Another weak system will move into the state Wednesday. Models are
mixed on whether we will get any rain from it. If so it probably 
won't be much, though there is a small portion of the ensembles
that show around a half inch of rain.

In any case, Thanksgiving is expected to be dry with some offshore
flow that will push temperatures into the 70s.

&&

.AVIATION...20/0414Z.

At 0005Z at KLAX, there was no marine layer nor an inversion.

Moderate to high confidence in all TAFs as rain from earlier today
clears out of the area. Expect any CIGs to be VFR, with only a 20%
chance of LIFR conds at KPRB early Friday morning. 

KLAX...High confidence in the 00Z TAF. There will be north winds
between 6 to 8 knots between 12Z-18Z Friday. No east wind 
component is expected during the fcst period.

KBUR...High confidence in the 00Z TAF. VFR conds expected.

&&

.MARINE...19/724 PM.

High confidence in dangerous ocean conditions through tonight  
due to a combination of gusty winds and large seas. Seas are
currently a combination of a large northwest swell and southwest 
wind swell. Large breaking waves may impact Morro Bay Harbor and 
to a lesser extent Ventura Harbor through tonight.

Conditions will improve through the day Friday and become relatively
mild through Saturday. A weak front will likely move across the 
coastal waters Sunday into Monday but impacts look minimal at 
this time. Looking ahead, another stronger cold front could 
impact the coastal waters Tuesday night into Wednesday with wind 
and rain. Large seas are also expected to return to the coastal 
waters around mid to late next week.

&&

.BEACHES...19/739 PM.

Large surf will create very dangerous rip currents and jetty 
conditions into Friday. High Surf Advisories remain in effect for
all beach areas.

Extremely high tides, likely record breaking, will occur over
Thanksgiving week (peaking Tuesday through Thanksgiving Day). 
Additional large westerly swells are becoming increasingly likely
next week as well. These swells have a good chance of producing a 
period of high surf for west facing beaches.

The combination of very high tides and increasing surf next week 
will likely lead to at least moderate-level, widespread coastal 
flooding issues across all coasts. There is potential for 
significant coastal flooding impacts if a larger swell overlaps 
with the timing of the extreme tides.

&&
